rationale:
Final design: iteration 5 (score 137.76, best measured), with base_speed set back to 1.8. I reject the 2.0 change, partly accepting the round-2 critique.

Why the 2.0 step is rejected: base_pwm = 4095 * min(1, base/2) reaches the 4095 ceiling at base_speed 2.0. At 1.8 there are about 410 counts of wheel-command headroom (roughly turn 1.2) before clipping. At 2.0 there is none on the outside wheel, so steering authority is lost in the direction that matters on bends. The critique's measured bend data points the same way: going from base 1.6 to 1.8 cut s-bend progress from 0.27 to 0.18 and slalom from 0.16 to 0.12, and the oval gain carried the net score. Line loss on the bends fell to 0.0 at 1.8, so the bend failure is off-track or lateral, not line loss.

What I kept: geometry, kp 2.8, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, sensor weights and last_direction line loss, all identical to iteration 5. I also accept the critique's point that the Evidence line about line loss of 0.65 to 0.8 was stale; the current measured value at 1.8 is 0.0 on the bends.

What I changed: nothing relative to iteration 5. Re-racing it is a control against the best known design, not a new test, so this iteration protects the score. I am not adopting 1.9 or 2.0 because neither has evidence.

Expected result: about 137.8, consistent with iterations 5 and 6. Next-round test, if I keep this line: a single-variable change to ki (0.1) or to one sensor footprint, judged against the bend mean scores (about 78 and 52) and the oval progress (about 0.55). I drop the footprint option unless it has a stated mechanism for the off-track end.
